To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new method, 4-RAPMUSIC, for the localization of brain sources from MEG and EEG recordings.
we have developed a new method for solving the inverse problem of EEG/MEG source localization.
the proposed 4-MUSIC (4-MUSIC) and 4-RAPMUSIC methods (4-RapMUS) are two high-resolution methods solving inverse problems, potentially ill-posed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of high resolution methods for localization of brain sources from MEG/EEG data.
the development of new high resolution methods to solve the inverse problem in EEG/MEG, with a special emphasis on the localization of brain current dipoles.
the design of new algorithms for the solution of the inverse problem in electroencephalography and magneto-ence-phalography.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4-RAPMUSIC approach is the most powerful and robust algorithm for solving the inverse problem of EEG source reconstruction.
the 4-MUSIC method is a powerful tool for source localization, but it is not able to solve ill-posed problems.
4-Rap-MUSIC is the most powerful algorithm for the localization of brain sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed 4-MUSIC/4-RapMUSCI approaches are very powerful tools for the estimation of the number of active sources and their localization.

we have proposed and tested a new approach for solving ill-posed inverse problems, the fourth order (4th) virtual array theory, which is based on the separability of a data transfer matrix as function of location and orientations of the sources.

the proposed 4-Rap-MUSIC method, which uses the virtual array theory and the deflation concept to account for the presence of possibly but not totally coherent brain sources, is the most powerful high resolution algorithm for the solution of the inverse problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 4-RAPMUSIC approach is a promising high resolution method that can be used to localize sources in realistic geometries and with unconstrained orientations.
the fourth order statistics can be used for the localization of brain current source with unconstrained orientations.
the 4-RAPMUSIC approach can be used to localize multiple current sources with unconstraint orientation from EEG data, and is robust against noise.
